what_failed: Producer inference on the Vultr CPU host could not complete within any tested bound. Cell b0/A (prompt 34,619 chars, ~8.6K estimated tokens) timed out at the frozen 300s producer timeout (measured wall 338.3s, no output). Cell b0/B then ran 7,115.8s (nearly 2 hours) without completing. A direct latency probe of the same b0/A prompt with a 900s curl budget also failed to produce any output file within >1000s, and the SSH connection was reset.
root_cause: CPU inference capacity on the Vultr host is insufficient for the real prompt sizes of this boundary set. The frozen computational budget was derived from the 009B pilot's measured 55.4s mean producer wall time, but that measurement was taken under different conditions (warm model, and critically the 009B producer prompts were ~2,050 actual prompt tokens per call - the 009B transcripts were capped far more aggressively in practice than the chars//4 estimate suggests). The actual b0/A prompt is 34,619 chars; at this host's CPU inference speed this exceeds 15 minutes per call. 40 such cells would take 10+ hours, far beyond the frozen 6h global timeout, and individual calls exceed the frozen 300s producer timeout by a wide margin.
measured_evidence: b0/A: F-TIMEOUT at 330s (wall 338.3s). b0/B: wall 7115.8s (no completion). Direct probe of b0/A prompt: no output after >1000s, SSH connection reset. Server up 5d14h, ollama processes running (3). Model qwen2.5:3b Q4_K_M, context_length 32768.
classification: F-INFRASTRUCTURE / F-TIMEOUT (systematic). Per the frozen protocol Phase 7 escalation rule: timeout > 20% of calls -> STOP and review the timeout budget. 2/2 attempted cells timed out (100%), far above the 20% threshold.
disposition_per_protocol: STOP. The pilot is stopped before Stage 4 completes. Per the frozen protocol: 'If the environment cannot support the full design at execution time, the pilot reports the shortfall rather than reducing the design.' No timeout was changed, no model substituted, no boundary skipped, no arm dropped. The frozen artifacts (boundaries, reference) remain frozen and valid.
what_i_did_wrong: The frozen computational budget (TASK_010_COMPUTATIONAL_BUDGET.md) extrapolated from 009B's measured per-cell wall time without validating that the actual prompt token counts would match. The chars//4 estimate (8.6K tokens for b0) vs the 009B measured ~2,050 actual producer prompt tokens discrepancy was visible in the 009B data (2,050 actual vs ~8,500 estimated) and was not investigated during protocol design. The budget section did note 'the only extrapolation in this document' but underestimated the risk.
protocol_gap_identified: The computational budget should have included a PRE-FLIGHT latency probe at the real prompt sizes (one producer call on the largest boundary) rather than relying on the 009B mean. This is a protocol defect to record for the next protocol version.
state_at_stop: Stage 1 PRE-FLIGHT: PASS. Stage 2 DATA FREEZE: FROZEN (10 boundaries, sha 35e42b8e). Stage 3 REFERENCE FREEZE: FROZEN (after gate-metric correction, recorded). Stage 4 ARM GENERATION: STOPPED - 2/40 cells attempted, 0 completed, 2 F-TIMEOUT. Stages 5-9: NOT STARTED.
retry_policy: Do NOT retry inference on this host. The capacity deficit is structural (CPU-only, 3B model, 8.6K-token prompts). Any resumption requires either (a) a new protocol version with a revised timeout budget and validated latency measurement, or (b) a different inference backend, which requires a new protocol version per the no-model-substitution rule.
